title: Probing Rotational Dynamics of Quark Gluon Plasma via Global Vorticity
comment: 8 pages and 6 captioned figures. Submitted for publication
summary: The findings on the spin polarization of $Λ$, $Ξ$, and $Ω$ hyperons and spin alignment of $K^{*0}$, $φ$, and $D^{*+}$ mesons in relativistic heavy-ion collision experiments at the RHIC and LHC facilities propose the emergence of a strong vorticity field produced in these collisions. Contemplating the potential impact of vorticity on the space-time evolution of deconfined QCD matter and its freeze-out properties, we aim to investigate its characteristics within the medium. We introduce a complementary and data-driven approach to quantify the global vorticity field by extracting it directly from the transverse momentum spectra of produced hadrons. Employing the experimental data for $Λ$, $Ξ$, $Ω$, $K^{*0}$, $K^{*\pm}$, $φ$, $ρ$, and $D^{*+}$ at mid-rapidity in Au+Au and Pb+Pb collisions over a wide range of beam energies, $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=7.7$ GeV-5.02 TeV, and centrality classes, we systematically examine spin-vorticity coupling in the medium. Our finding on the magnitude of the extracted vorticity is consistent with values deduced from $Λ$ and $\barΛ$ polarization measurements using statistical thermal models under the non-relativistic limit. Notably, we observe a prominent particle-species dependence of the vorticity, as well as a non-trivial variation with collision centrality and beam energy. These results indicate that vorticity-driven spin phenomena are sensitive to hadron structure and freeze-out dynamics, providing new constraints on the rotational properties of the QCD matter.

AI.tldr: A data-driven approach extracts global vorticity from transverse momentum spectra of various hadrons in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, revealing particle-species dependence and non-trivial variations with centrality and beam energy.
AI.motivation: Spin polarization measurements of hyperons and spin alignment of mesons suggest strong vorticity fields in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, motivating investigation of vorticity's impact on QCD matter evolution and freeze-out properties.
AI.method: Complementary data-driven approach quantifying global vorticity by extracting it directly from transverse momentum spectra of produced hadrons (Λ, Ξ, Ω, K*0, K*±, φ, ρ, D*+) at mid-rapidity across wide range of beam energies (7.7 GeV-5.02 TeV) and centrality classes in Au+Au and Pb+Pb collisions.
AI.result: Extracted vorticity magnitude consistent with values from Λ and Λ̄ polarization measurements using statistical thermal models; shows prominent particle-species dependence and non-trivial variation with collision centrality and beam energy.
AI.conclusion: Vorticity-driven spin phenomena are sensitive to hadron structure and freeze-out dynamics, providing new constraints on rotational properties of QCD matter in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

title: Next-to-Leading-Order QCD Predictions for the $Σ$ Dirac Form Factors
summary: In this work, we compute the next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to the Dirac electromagnetic form factors of the $Σ$ hyperons within the hard-collinear factorization framework at leading power. The corresponding short-distance coefficient functions are extracted from the relevant seven-point partonic correlation functions. We find that the one-loop radiative corrections to the leading-twist hard-scattering contributions are numerically significant over a broad range of momentum transfer. Combining the perturbatively calculated hard kernels with nonperturbative $Σ$ distribution amplitudes determined from lattice QCD, we present state-of-the-art theoretical predictions for the $Σ$ hyperon electromagnetic form factors.

AI.tldr: NLO QCD corrections to Σ hyperon electromagnetic form factors computed using hard-collinear factorization at leading power, with significant radiative corrections and state-of-the-art predictions combining perturbative hard kernels with lattice QCD distribution amplitudes.
AI.motivation: To provide precise theoretical predictions for Σ hyperon electromagnetic form factors by computing next-to-leading-order QCD corrections within the hard-collinear factorization framework, addressing the numerical significance of radiative corrections and combining perturbative calculations with nonperturbative lattice QCD inputs.
AI.method: Hard-collinear factorization at leading power; extraction of short-distance coefficient functions from seven-point partonic correlation functions; computation of one-loop radiative corrections to leading-twist hard-scattering contributions; combination of perturbatively calculated hard kernels with nonperturbative Σ distribution amplitudes determined from lattice QCD.
AI.result: One-loop radiative corrections to leading-twist hard-scattering contributions are numerically significant over a broad range of momentum transfer; state-of-the-art theoretical predictions for Σ hyperon electromagnetic form factors are presented.
AI.conclusion: The work provides improved theoretical precision for Σ hyperon electromagnetic form factors through NLO QCD corrections within hard-collinear factorization, demonstrating the importance of radiative corrections and the successful combination of perturbative and lattice QCD approaches.

title: Current status and prospects of light bino-higgsino dark matter in natural SUSY
summary: Given recent advancements in dark matter (DM) search experiments, particularly the latest LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) direct detection (DD) results, we systematically investigate the light bino-higgsino DM scenario within the natural supersymmetric framework. Requiring the electroweak fine-tuning parameter $Δ_{\text{EW}} < 30$ fixes the higgsino mass parameter in the range $|μ| \in [100, 350]$ GeV, while we extend the bino mass to $M_1 \in [10, 350]$ GeV. Incorporating constraints from Higgs physics, rare $B$ decays, LEP limits, and DD experiments, we find that part of the parameter space remains viable. However, the relic density of neutralino DM necessarily lies below the observed Planck value, contributing at most $\sim 2\%$ of the total DM abundance. Some of the surviving parameter space is already excluded by current 13 TeV LHC searches, while the future 14 TeV HL-LHC with 3000 fb$^{-1}$ luminosity will probe the remaining region.

AI.tldr: Light bino-higgsino DM scenario in natural SUSY is systematically studied under LZ constraints, finding viable parameter space but with relic density contributing only ~2% of total DM abundance, and HL-LHC will probe remaining regions.
AI.motivation: Recent advancements in dark matter direct detection experiments, particularly LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) results, motivate systematic investigation of light bino-higgsino DM in natural supersymmetry to understand viable parameter space under current constraints.
AI.method: Systematic investigation of light bino-higgsino DM scenario within natural SUSY framework with electroweak fine-tuning Δ_EW < 30, fixing higgsino mass parameter |μ| ∈ [100, 350] GeV and extending bino mass M_1 ∈ [10, 350] GeV. Incorporates constraints from Higgs physics, rare B decays, LEP limits, and direct detection experiments.
AI.result: Part of parameter space remains viable, but neutralino DM relic density is necessarily below observed Planck value, contributing at most ~2% of total DM abundance. Some surviving parameter space already excluded by 13 TeV LHC searches, while future 14 TeV HL-LHC with 3000 fb⁻¹ luminosity will probe remaining region.
AI.conclusion: Light bino-higgsino DM in natural SUSY is severely constrained, with relic density insufficient to account for total observed DM abundance, and future HL-LHC experiments will provide crucial tests for remaining viable parameter space.

title: Towards 3D CFT Cartography with the Stress Tensor Bootstrap
summary: We present new numerical results on the space of local, unitary, parity-preserving conformal field theories (CFTs) in three dimensions from the stress tensor bootstrap. In bounds maximizing certain OPE coefficients, we find a plethora of sharp features, such as kinks and ridges, as a function of scaling dimensions. We show that some of these features correspond to known theories, but there are many others that are equally strong but do not match known CFTs. We argue that these features are robust to raising numerical order and could then correspond to numerous as yet unknown CFTs. We conclude in proposing a program of "CFT cartography": the systematic exploration of the landscape of CFTs without individual theory targets in mind.

AI.tldr: Numerical bootstrap study of 3D parity-preserving CFTs reveals many sharp features (kinks, ridges) in OPE coefficient bounds, some matching known theories but many potentially representing unknown CFTs, motivating systematic "CFT cartography" exploration.
AI.motivation: To systematically explore the landscape of three-dimensional local, unitary, parity-preserving conformal field theories using numerical bootstrap methods, moving beyond targeting specific known theories to discover potentially unknown CFTs.
AI.method: Stress tensor bootstrap approach with numerical calculations maximizing certain OPE coefficients, analyzing bounds as functions of scaling dimensions, and identifying sharp features (kinks, ridges) that persist at higher numerical orders.
AI.result: Discovery of numerous sharp features in OPE coefficient bounds, with some corresponding to known CFTs but many equally strong features not matching any known theories, suggesting these could represent unknown CFTs.
AI.conclusion: Proposes "CFT cartography" program for systematic exploration of CFT landscape without predetermined theory targets, based on robustness of discovered features to higher numerical orders.

title: Scale invariant radiative neutrino mass model
summary: We propose a scale invariant radiative neutrino mass model with custodial symmetry. Masses of an inert doublet scalar and right-handed neutrinos are induced by a vacuum expectation value (VEV) of a singlet scalar caused through the Coleman-Weinberg mechanism. It violates spontaneously both the custodial symmetry and the scale invariance. The weak scale can take a suppressed value compared with the singlet scalar VEV because of the custodial symmetry. In this framework we study phenomenological consequences for neutrino mass, dark matter and baryon number asymmetry. Since the required dark matter abundance cannot be explained by a neutral component of the inert doublet scalar, the lightest right-handed neutrino should be dark matter. Mass of the dark matter is predicted to be less than $O(1)$ MeV and baryon number asymmetry could be explained through resonant leptogenesis.

AI.tldr: Scale-invariant radiative neutrino mass model with custodial symmetry where inert doublet and right-handed neutrino masses arise from singlet scalar VEV via Coleman-Weinberg mechanism, predicting MeV-scale dark matter and resonant leptogenesis.
AI.motivation: To construct a scale-invariant framework that simultaneously addresses neutrino mass generation, dark matter, and baryon asymmetry while explaining the hierarchy between electroweak scale and new physics scale through custodial symmetry.
AI.method: Introduce an inert doublet scalar and right-handed neutrinos whose masses are generated by a singlet scalar VEV via Coleman-Weinberg mechanism, spontaneously breaking both custodial symmetry and scale invariance; use custodial symmetry to suppress weak scale relative to singlet VEV.
AI.result: The inert doublet cannot provide sufficient dark matter density, requiring the lightest right-handed neutrino as dark matter with mass below O(1) MeV; baryon asymmetry can be explained through resonant leptogenesis.
AI.conclusion: The proposed scale-invariant model with custodial symmetry successfully connects neutrino mass generation, dark matter, and baryogenesis while naturally explaining the electroweak hierarchy, predicting MeV-scale right-handed neutrino dark matter and viable leptogenesis.

title: Physical Predictions in Closed Quantum Gravity
summary: Recent developments in gravitational path integrals indicate that the nonperturbative physical Hilbert space of a closed universe is one-dimensional within each superselection sector. This raises a basic puzzle: how can a unique quantum-gravity state give rise to semiclassical physics, measurement outcomes, and classical probabilities? In this paper, we develop a framework in which nontrivial and statistically stable predictions emerge despite the one-dimensionality of the fully constrained Hilbert space. The key idea is to extract physical predictions in an enlarged, unconstrained Hilbert space by conditioning on observational data. We show that partial observability -- reflecting the limited access of observers to the degrees of freedom of the universe -- suppresses ensemble fluctuations associated with microscopic structure in the gravitational path integral, thereby restoring semiclassical predictability with exponential accuracy. We formulate the construction explicitly including contributions from the Hartle--Hawking no-boundary state, define a gauge-invariant Hilbert space for observations via a density operator, and generalize the formalism to conditioning on histories, clarifying the emergence of classical probabilities and an effective arrow of time. Finally, we explore whether this framework can support a realistic cosmology and identify assumptions that the underlying theory of quantum gravity must satisfy.

AI.tldr: A framework for extracting physical predictions from one-dimensional quantum gravity Hilbert spaces by conditioning on observational data, enabling semiclassical physics despite minimal state space.
AI.motivation: Resolve the puzzle of how a one-dimensional Hilbert space in closed-universe quantum gravity can give rise to semiclassical physics, measurement outcomes, and classical probabilities.
AI.method: Develop framework using enlarged unconstrained Hilbert space with conditioning on observational data; partial observability suppresses ensemble fluctuations; includes Hartle-Hawking no-boundary state contributions; defines gauge-invariant Hilbert space via density operator; generalizes to history conditioning.
AI.result: Partial observability restores semiclassical predictability with exponential accuracy by suppressing microscopic ensemble fluctuations; framework enables emergence of classical probabilities and effective arrow of time.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides mechanism for nontrivial predictions despite one-dimensional Hilbert space; identifies necessary assumptions for underlying quantum gravity theory to support realistic cosmology.

title: An imprint of intrinsic quark--gluon correlations: a nonmonotonic feature in $e(x)$
summary: We present the first rainbow-ladder Dyson-Schwinger equations study of the pion's chiral-odd, twist-3 parton distribution $e_{\rm q}(x)$. By deriving a novel Dyson-Schwinger equation for the pion's quark-quark correlation matrix, we simultaneously extract from it both the unpolarized twist-2 parton distribution function $f_{\rm q}(x)$ and the twist-3 distribution $e_{\rm q}(x)$. Our results show that chiral symmetry strongly suppresses the twist-2 component of $e_{\rm q}(x)$, leaving the genuine twist-3 quark-gluon component dominant and featuring a node. We therefore argue that the genuine twist-3 term can make a substantial contribution to hadronic $e(x)$, producing a nonmonotonic structure that is a clear imprint of intrinsic quark-gluon correlations. We point out that the existence of a hump-like feature is compatible with, although not uniquely indicated by, recent proton extractions and awaits more precise determination.

AI.tldr: First Dyson-Schwinger equations study of pion's chiral-odd twist-3 parton distribution e_q(x) reveals chiral symmetry suppression of twist-2 component, leaving genuine twist-3 quark-gluon term dominant with nodal structure.
AI.motivation: To investigate the pion's chiral-odd, twist-3 parton distribution e_q(x) using Dyson-Schwinger equations, addressing the interplay between twist-2 and genuine twist-3 components and their relation to chiral symmetry and quark-gluon correlations.
AI.method: Developed novel Dyson-Schwinger equation for pion's quark-quark correlation matrix within rainbow-ladder approximation, enabling simultaneous extraction of both twist-2 PDF f_q(x) and twist-3 distribution e_q(x).
AI.result: Chiral symmetry strongly suppresses twist-2 component of e_q(x), making genuine twist-3 quark-gluon component dominant with nodal structure; produces nonmonotonic hump-like feature indicating intrinsic quark-gluon correlations.
AI.conclusion: Genuine twist-3 term can substantially contribute to hadronic e(x), creating nonmonotonic structure as clear imprint of intrinsic quark-gluon correlations; hump-like feature compatible with recent proton extractions but requires more precise determination.

title: Holographic Dark Matter
summary: Cold dark matter may be a fluid (or plasma) residing in a strongly-interacting hidden sector, rather than a population of weakly-coupled particles. Such a scenario admits a holographic description in terms of a cosmological braneworld embedded in the linear dilaton five-dimensional (5D) spacetime. In this framework, dark matter originates from the linear dilaton bulk black hole, whose phase we show to be thermodynamically favored at all temperatures. We present a natural freeze-in mechanism for the production of holographic dark matter, in which the bulk black hole is fed by energy leaking from the brane after inflation. Our model is characterized by two free parameters, one of which, the position of the black hole horizon, is fixed by the observed dark matter abundance. The remaining parameter, the 5D Planck scale $M_5$, is consistent with all current experimental bounds provided that $M_5\gtrsim 3\times 10^5$ TeV.

AI.tldr: Holographic dark matter model where cold dark matter is a fluid from a linear dilaton bulk black hole in a braneworld cosmology, with freeze-in production from brane energy leakage.
AI.motivation: To explore alternative dark matter scenarios beyond weakly-coupled particles, specifically fluid/plasma dark matter residing in a strongly-interacting hidden sector that admits a holographic description.
AI.method: Uses a cosmological braneworld embedded in linear dilaton 5D spacetime, with dark matter originating from the linear dilaton bulk black hole. Implements a freeze-in mechanism where the bulk black hole is fed by energy leaking from the brane after inflation.
AI.result: The bulk black hole phase is thermodynamically favored at all temperatures. The model has two parameters: black hole horizon position (fixed by observed dark matter abundance) and 5D Planck scale M5, which must satisfy M5 ≳ 3×10^5 TeV to be consistent with current experimental bounds.
AI.conclusion: Holographic dark matter from a linear dilaton bulk black hole provides a viable alternative to particle dark matter, with a natural freeze-in production mechanism and parameter space consistent with observational constraints.

title: Factorization formula connecting the $Λ_Q$ LCDA in QCD and boosted HQET
summary: Light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) are essential to precision phenomenology in heavy baryon decays. In this work, we derive a factorization formula connecting the leading-twist QCD LCDA to the boosted HQET LCDA of the $Λ_Q$ baryon in the peak region. We demonstrate a significant simplification of the matching procedure by applying the method-of-regions to perturbative calculations. With this simplification, we calculate the required one-loop perturbative corrections to the QCD and boosted HQET LCDAs in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme, and thereby obtain the one-loop jet function that serves as the matching kernel in the factorization formula. This result provides a critical step toward lattice QCD calculation of heavy baryon LCDAs in the future.

AI.tldr: Derivation of factorization formula connecting QCD and HQET LCDAs for Λ_Q baryons, with simplified matching via method-of-regions and one-loop jet function calculation.
AI.motivation: Light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) are crucial for precision phenomenology in heavy baryon decays, but their calculation requires connecting QCD and HQET frameworks, particularly for Λ_Q baryons in the peak region.
AI.method: Applied method-of-regions to perturbative calculations to simplify matching procedure, derived factorization formula connecting leading-twist QCD LCDA to boosted HQET LCDA, and calculated one-loop perturbative corrections to both LCDAs in the MS-bar scheme.
AI.result: Obtained one-loop jet function that serves as matching kernel in the factorization formula, demonstrating significant simplification of the matching procedure through method-of-regions approach.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a critical step toward future lattice QCD calculations of heavy baryon LCDAs by establishing the factorization framework and matching kernel between QCD and HQET descriptions.

title: Holographic observables in TsT deformations of confining theories
summary: We construct new families of type-IIB supergravity solutions by employing TsT transformations on the ten-dimensional geometry that arises after the uplift of the five-dimensional soliton solution of Anabalón, Nastase, and Oyarzo. In particular, we identify two marginal and two dipole deformations of the uplifted geometry. We then analyse a plethora of holographic observables -- including Wilson loops, `t~Hooft loops, Page charges, entanglement entropy, and central charge -- and compare their behaviour across the different deformed backgrounds.

AI.tldr: TsT transformations generate new type-IIB supergravity solutions from uplifted 5D soliton, yielding marginal and dipole deformations; holographic observables analyzed across deformed backgrounds.
AI.motivation: To construct new families of type-IIB supergravity solutions by applying TsT transformations to uplifted geometries from known 5D soliton solutions, and to systematically study how various holographic observables behave under different deformations.
AI.method: Employ TsT (T-duality-shift-T-duality) transformations on the ten-dimensional geometry obtained by uplifting the five-dimensional soliton solution of Anabalón, Nastase, and Oyarzo. Specifically identify two marginal and two dipole deformations of the uplifted geometry.
AI.result: Construction of new families of type-IIB supergravity solutions through TsT transformations. Analysis of holographic observables including Wilson loops, 't Hooft loops, Page charges, entanglement entropy, and central charge reveals their behavior across different deformed backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: TsT transformations provide a systematic method to generate deformed supergravity solutions from uplifted geometries, enabling comparative study of holographic observables across different deformation types, with implications for understanding deformed holographic dualities.

title: Limits on the Carroll-Field-Jackiw electrodynamics from geomagnetic data
comment: 58 pages, 16 figures. Constructive comments are welcome
summary: Lorentz-symmetry violation may be described via the CPT-odd, dimension-3, Carroll-Field-Jackiw term, which couples the electromagnetic fields to a constant 4-vector $k_{\rm AF}$ selecting a preferred direction in spacetime. We solve the field equations using the Green's method for a static point-like magnetic dipole and find the $k_{\rm AF}$-dependent corrections to the standard dipolar magnetic field that strongly dominates the near-Earth magnetic field. Given the very good agreement between current models and ground- and satellite-based geomagnetic data, our strongest constraints on the components of $k_{\rm AF}$ in the Sun-centered frame read $|(k_{\rm AF})_Z| \lesssim 4 \times 10^{-25} \, {\rm GeV}$ for $|(k_{\rm AF})_X|, |(k_{\rm AF})_Y| \lesssim 10^{-24} \, {\rm GeV}$ at the two-sigma level. This represents an improvement of about four orders of magnitude over earlier bounds based on other geophysical phenomena.

AI.tldr: Analysis of Lorentz violation via Carroll-Field-Jackiw term using Earth's magnetic field data yields improved constraints on CPT-odd parameter k_AF.
AI.motivation: To test Lorentz symmetry violation through the CPT-odd Carroll-Field-Jackiw term by analyzing its effects on Earth's magnetic field, leveraging precise geomagnetic measurements.
AI.method: Solve field equations using Green's method for a static point-like magnetic dipole, calculate k_AF-dependent corrections to standard dipolar field, and compare with ground- and satellite-based geomagnetic data.
AI.result: Strongest constraints: |(k_AF)_Z| ≲ 4×10⁻²⁵ GeV and |(k_AF)_X|, |(k_AF)_Y| ≲ 10⁻²⁴ GeV at 2σ level, representing ~4 orders of magnitude improvement over previous geophysical bounds.
AI.conclusion: Earth's magnetic field provides a sensitive probe for Lorentz violation, yielding significantly improved constraints on CPT-odd parameters through precise geomagnetic measurements.

title: Fixing EFT equations with a reservoir model
summary: Effective Field Theories with higher derivatives often yield equations of motion which define ill-posed problems. We present a method for enhancing control on such theories by coupling them to a field living in one extra dimension. The resulting action principle helps to define a well-posed problem introducing a mechanism to control UV behavior. Physically this is achieved by dissipating the energy in the short-wavelength modes into the extra dimension. We examine the resulting dynamics and compare it to alternative proposals for studying such theories in the non-linear regime.

AI.tldr: A method for controlling ill-posed higher-derivative effective field theories by coupling them to an extra-dimensional field, dissipating UV energy into the extra dimension.
AI.motivation: Higher-derivative effective field theories often lead to ill-posed equations of motion that lack proper UV control and well-defined dynamics.
AI.method: Couple the higher-derivative theory to a field living in one extra dimension, creating an action principle that introduces a mechanism to control UV behavior through energy dissipation into the extra dimension.
AI.result: The approach yields well-posed problems by dissipating energy from short-wavelength modes into the extra dimension, providing UV control for higher-derivative theories.
AI.conclusion: The extra-dimensional coupling method offers a viable approach to study higher-derivative effective field theories in the non-linear regime with proper UV control, compared to alternative proposals.

title: Measuring neutrino mixing above 1 TeV with astrophysical neutrinos
summary: We assess the potential for measuring neutrino mixing parameters at energies above 1~TeV, for the first time, using the flavor composition of TeV--PeV astrophysical neutrinos, i.e., the proportion of $ν_e$, $ν_μ$, and $ν_τ$. Today, flavor measurements inferred from the 11.4-year IceCube Medium Energy Starting Events sample are insufficient to constrain the mixing parameters due to limited statistics, challenges in flavor identification, and uncertainty in neutrino production. Yet, upcoming multi-neutrino-telescope observations -- even using only existing telescopes -- may achieve sensitivity to $θ_{23}$ and $θ_{13}$ when combined with traditional oscillation experiments. We establish the current status and future prospects for testing the three-flavor mixing framework in the previously unexplored TeV--PeV regime and quantify the minimum detectable size of flavor-modifying beyond-Standard-Model effects, providing a roadmap for high-energy neutrino mixing measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper assesses the potential for measuring neutrino mixing parameters at TeV-PeV energies using astrophysical neutrino flavor composition, establishing current limitations and future prospects for testing three-flavor mixing in this high-energy regime.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to explore neutrino mixing parameters at energies above 1 TeV using astrophysical neutrinos, which represents a previously unexplored energy regime for flavor measurements, potentially providing new constraints on mixing parameters and beyond-Standard-Model effects.
AI.method: The method involves analyzing the flavor composition (proportions of ν_e, ν_μ, ν_τ) of TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrinos from the IceCube Medium Energy Starting Events sample, assessing current limitations, and projecting future sensitivity from multi-neutrino-telescope observations combined with traditional oscillation experiments.
AI.result: Current 11.4-year IceCube data is insufficient to constrain mixing parameters due to limited statistics, flavor identification challenges, and neutrino production uncertainties. However, future multi-telescope observations may achieve sensitivity to θ_{23} and θ_{13} when combined with traditional experiments.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a roadmap for high-energy neutrino mixing measurements, quantifying the minimum detectable size of flavor-modifying beyond-Standard-Model effects and demonstrating the potential for testing three-flavor mixing in the TeV-PeV regime using upcoming astrophysical neutrino observations.

title: Braneworlds in Constant and Accelerated Motion and Their Causal Characteristics
summary: We generalize prior work on the signatures of bulk signals detected by brane-based observers in a spacetime with a compactified dimension. When such braneworlds move with constant velocities or constant proper accelerations in the extra dimension, the observers may witness apparent superluminal signaling. Our analysis includes tilted branes that are partially wrapped along the compact dimension. We identify parameters that help characterize various scenarios. Despite the apparent superluminality of bulk signals, we show that anisotropies in their propagation relative to the brane-based observer preserve causality. Some of the effects studied here could be the basis for alternative cosmological models, as well as observable signatures of braneworld scenarios.

AI.tldr: Brane-based observers in compactified dimensions may detect apparent superluminal bulk signals when branes move with constant velocities or accelerations, but causality is preserved through propagation anisotropies.
AI.motivation: To generalize prior work on bulk signal signatures detected by brane-based observers in spacetimes with compactified dimensions, particularly when branes move with constant velocities or accelerations, and to explore implications for cosmological models and braneworld signatures.
AI.method: Analysis includes tilted branes partially wrapped along compact dimensions, identification of characterizing parameters, and examination of bulk signal propagation relative to brane-based observers in various motion scenarios.
AI.result: Observers may witness apparent superluminal signaling, but anisotropies in bulk signal propagation relative to the brane preserve causality; parameters characterizing different scenarios are identified.
AI.conclusion: Despite apparent superluminality, causality is maintained through propagation anisotropies; effects studied could form basis for alternative cosmological models and observable signatures of braneworld scenarios.

title: A Convergent Kinetic-Term Perturbation Expansion for phi4 Theory
summary: We revisit scalar $φ^4$ theory and construct a reorganized perturbative expansion in which the kinetic operator, rather than the quartic interaction, is treated as the perturbation. Starting from the exactly solvable $0$-dimensional model, we show that the resulting series is convergent for positive coupling and can be written as an expansion in negative powers of the quartic coupling $λ$. We extend the construction to higher-dimensional field theory using an auxiliary field, and we formulate a discrete lattice version in which multi-site contributions are systematically organized. We explicitly compute the leading terms in the expansion, study their continuum limit, and compare against brute-force numerical evaluations of the partition function. We discuss the relation of this expansion to standard weak-coupling perturbation theory, strong-coupling expansions, and resummation techniques, and we outline possible applications to nonperturbative studies of scalar field theories.

AI.tldr: A novel perturbative expansion for φ⁴ theory where the kinetic term is treated as perturbation rather than the quartic interaction, yielding convergent series in negative powers of coupling λ.
AI.motivation: To develop an alternative perturbative framework for scalar φ⁴ theory that converges for positive coupling, addressing limitations of standard weak-coupling perturbation theory and providing new analytical tools for nonperturbative studies.
AI.method: Reorganize perturbation theory by treating the kinetic operator as perturbation instead of quartic interaction; start from exactly solvable 0D model; extend to higher dimensions using auxiliary field; formulate discrete lattice version with systematic organization of multi-site contributions.
AI.result: The expansion converges for positive coupling λ and can be expressed as series in negative powers of λ; leading terms computed explicitly; continuum limit studied; results compared against numerical evaluations of partition function.
AI.conclusion: This alternative expansion provides convergent perturbative framework for φ⁴ theory, connects to standard weak-coupling perturbation theory and strong-coupling expansions, and offers potential applications for nonperturbative studies of scalar field theories.

title: Effects of the symmetry energy slope on magnetized neutron stars
summary: In this work, we study the effect of the symmetry slope on the observables of weakly and strongly magnetized neutron stars within the chaotic magnetic field approximation. We investigate the impact of the symmetry energy slope in the equation of state, as well as on the observables of neutron stars, by calculating their masses, radii, redshifts, tidal deformabilities, and fundamental-mode gravitational-wave frequencies.

AI.tldr: Study examines how symmetry energy slope affects neutron star properties under chaotic magnetic field approximation, analyzing mass, radius, redshift, tidal deformability, and gravitational-wave frequencies.
AI.motivation: To understand how the symmetry energy slope parameter in the nuclear equation of state influences observable properties of neutron stars, particularly in the presence of magnetic fields, which is crucial for interpreting astrophysical observations and gravitational wave signals.
AI.method: Using chaotic magnetic field approximation, the study calculates neutron star properties including masses, radii, redshifts, tidal deformabilities, and fundamental-mode gravitational-wave frequencies while varying the symmetry energy slope parameter in the equation of state.
AI.result: The symmetry energy slope significantly impacts neutron star observables, with different slopes leading to variations in mass-radius relations, tidal deformabilities, and gravitational-wave frequencies for both weakly and strongly magnetized neutron stars.
AI.conclusion: Symmetry energy slope is a critical parameter that must be carefully constrained in equation of state models, as it substantially affects neutron star observables and their interpretation from astrophysical measurements, especially in magnetized environments.

title: Defect Approach to Giant Graviton Dynamics
summary: We develop a framework of zero dimensional defects for analyzing light-light-heavy-heavy (LLHH) correlators in conformal field theories. We specifically apply this formalism to correlators of giant gravitons in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills to probe the nontrivial physics beyond planarity. By combining this framework with bootstrap techniques, we compute all four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons of arbitrary dimensions. We identify a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry -- a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry -- present at both strong and weak coupling, which allows these correlators to be packaged into a single generating function. Furthermore, we perform a systematic OPE analysis of the strong-coupling correlators, extracting the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for the defect-channel double-particle operators. Finally, we argue that the defect perspective provides the natural nonperturbative description for any LLHH correlator by showing that four-point conformal blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.

AI.tldr: Develops a zero-dimensional defect framework for analyzing LLHH correlators in CFTs, applied to giant gravitons in N=4 SYM to probe beyond-planar physics, revealing hidden defect symmetry and computing strong-coupling four-point functions.
AI.motivation: To probe nontrivial physics beyond planarity in conformal field theories, specifically in N=4 SYM, by analyzing light-light-heavy-heavy (LLHH) correlators involving giant gravitons, which requires going beyond standard planar techniques.
AI.method: Develops a zero-dimensional defect framework combined with bootstrap techniques; applies this to compute four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons; identifies hidden defect symmetry; performs systematic OPE analysis of strong-coupling correlators.
AI.result: Computed all four-point functions at strong coupling for specified operators; identified a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry (defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry) present at both strong and weak coupling; extracted complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for defect-channel double-particle operators; showed defect perspective provides natural nonperturbative description for LLHH correlators.
AI.conclusion: The defect framework provides a powerful approach for analyzing LLHH correlators beyond planarity, revealing hidden symmetries and enabling nonperturbative descriptions through reduction of four-point conformal blocks to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.

title: Maxwell theories along the light track: Null Formalism in extended electrodynamics
summary: We develop a differential-form approach to systematically derive the Newman-Penrose null-tetrad equations for Lorentz-violating extensions of Maxwell electrodynamics. The coordinate-independent nature of differential forms allows the actions and corresponding field equations of the theory to be expressed compactly and enables a systematic and transparent derivation of first-order equations in the Newman-Penrose formalism. Within this formalism, we explicitly present a simple algebraic construction for the gauge invariant extended Maxwell actions that avoids explicit index manipulations up to mass dimension six. The combined scheme of differential-form approach and Newman-Penrose formalism offers an efficient tool for analyzing Lorentz-violating effects on asymptotic photon propagation and polarization.

AI.tldr: A differential-form approach to derive Newman-Penrose equations for Lorentz-violating Maxwell electrodynamics, enabling systematic analysis of photon propagation and polarization effects.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic framework for analyzing Lorentz-violating extensions of Maxwell electrodynamics, particularly for studying asymptotic photon propagation and polarization effects in a coordinate-independent manner.
AI.method: Uses differential-form approach to derive Newman-Penrose null-tetrad equations for Lorentz-violating Maxwell electrodynamics. The coordinate-independent nature of differential forms allows compact expression of actions and field equations, enabling systematic derivation of first-order equations in Newman-Penrose formalism.
AI.result: Presents a simple algebraic construction for gauge invariant extended Maxwell actions up to mass dimension six without explicit index manipulations. The combined differential-form and Newman-Penrose formalism provides an efficient tool for analyzing Lorentz-violating effects.
AI.conclusion: The differential-form approach combined with Newman-Penrose formalism offers an efficient, systematic framework for studying Lorentz-violating effects in Maxwell electrodynamics, particularly for analyzing asymptotic photon propagation and polarization.

title: Higher Connection in Open String Field Theory
summary: We define a 2-form connection in the space of classical solutions of the bosonic open string field theory, using the open string star product and integration. The corresponding higher holonomies and the 3-form curvature are new observables invariant under the infinite-dimensional gauge algebra of open string field theory. The definition is analogous to that of Berry phase in quantum mechanics and is motivated by recent studies on higher Berry phase in condensed matter physics and quantum field theory. We suggest identifying this 2-form connection with the Kalb-Ramond $B$-field of the closed string background at least in favorable situations. Also discussed are sigma models whose target space is the moduli space of conformal boundary conditions of a two-dimensional CFT with the $B$-field given by a cousin of this 2-form connection.

AI.tldr: The paper defines a 2-form connection in bosonic open string field theory using star product and integration, creating new gauge-invariant observables analogous to Berry phase, potentially identifying it with the Kalb-Ramond B-field.
AI.motivation: Motivated by recent studies on higher Berry phase in condensed matter physics and quantum field theory, the authors aim to construct analogous geometric structures in open string field theory, potentially connecting open string dynamics to closed string backgrounds.
AI.method: Define a 2-form connection in the space of classical solutions of bosonic open string field theory using the open string star product and integration. Construct corresponding higher holonomies and 3-form curvature as gauge-invariant observables under the infinite-dimensional gauge algebra of open string field theory.
AI.result: New gauge-invariant observables (higher holonomies and 3-form curvature) are constructed. The 2-form connection is suggested to be identified with the Kalb-Ramond B-field of the closed string background in favorable situations. Also discuss sigma models with target space as moduli space of conformal boundary conditions with B-field given by a cousin of this 2-form connection.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a geometric structure in open string field theory analogous to Berry phase, providing new observables and suggesting connections between open string dynamics and closed string backgrounds via identification with the Kalb-Ramond B-field.

title: Establishing the Primary HEFT as a Precision Benchmark for UV-HEFT Matching
summary: We match the real Higgs triplet model (RHTM) onto HEFT under different parameter choices and power-counting schemes, thereby obtaining several representative HEFT formulations and clarifying their relations. We establish the primary HEFT (pHEFT) as a benchmark framework, demonstrating that alternative HEFT constructions can be systematically derived from it. A key advantage of the pHEFT construction is its parameter choice, which maintains linear relations between the UV Lagrangian parameters and squared heavy masses. By strictly employing the inverse squared heavy masses as the expansion parameters without imposing additional constraints, pHEFT preserves maximal ultraviolet (UV) information and ensures higher perturbative accuracy by avoiding the additional truncations inherent in more complex, non-linear formulations or extra constraints. Through the analysis of the $Z_2$-symmetric real singlet model and the 2HDM, we illustrate the criteria for identifying viable primary HEFT constructions in UV models with scalar extensions. Furthermore, for the first time, we derive the HEFT operators of the RHTM involving fermions.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a systematic approach to derive HEFT formulations from UV models like the real Higgs triplet model, establishing primary HEFT as a benchmark framework that preserves maximal UV information through proper parameter choices and expansion schemes.
AI.motivation: To establish a systematic framework for matching UV models (particularly the real Higgs triplet model) to HEFT, clarifying relations between different HEFT formulations and identifying optimal parameter choices that preserve UV information while maintaining perturbative accuracy.
AI.method: Matching the real Higgs triplet model onto HEFT under different parameter choices and power-counting schemes; establishing primary HEFT as a benchmark; analyzing Z₂-symmetric real singlet model and 2HDM to identify criteria for viable primary HEFT constructions; deriving HEFT operators for RHTM involving fermions for the first time.
AI.result: Obtained several representative HEFT formulations and clarified their relations; demonstrated that alternative HEFT constructions can be systematically derived from primary HEFT; established criteria for identifying viable primary HEFT constructions in UV models with scalar extensions; derived the first HEFT operators for RHTM involving fermions.
AI.conclusion: Primary HEFT serves as an optimal benchmark framework that preserves maximal UV information through linear parameter-mass relations and proper expansion in inverse squared heavy masses, avoiding additional truncations and ensuring higher perturbative accuracy compared to more complex formulations.

title: On massive higher spins and gravity. IV. Arbitrary spin
summary: In this paper, we investigate gravitational interactions of massive fields with arbitrary integer and half-integer spin, trying to construct a vertex that contains both standard minimal and non-minimal interaction terms necessary to make the vertex gauge invariant. We propose an ansatz for these non-minimal terms and show that it leads to a unique solution that correctly reproduces our previous results for spins 5/2, 3 and 7/2, including all possible partially massless limits.

AI.tldr: Construction of gauge-invariant gravitational vertices for massive fields of arbitrary integer/half-integer spin, with both minimal and non-minimal terms, reproducing known results for spins 5/2, 3, and 7/2 including partially massless limits.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic framework for gravitational interactions of massive fields with arbitrary spin, addressing the need for both minimal and non-minimal interaction terms to achieve gauge invariance, which is crucial for consistent field theories in curved spacetime.
AI.method: Propose an ansatz for non-minimal interaction terms in gravitational vertices, then demonstrate that this ansatz leads to a unique solution that satisfies gauge invariance requirements and reproduces previously established results for specific spin cases.
AI.result: The proposed ansatz successfully yields a unique gauge-invariant vertex construction that correctly reproduces known results for spins 5/2, 3, and 7/2, including all possible partially massless limits, validating the approach for arbitrary spin fields.
AI.conclusion: The developed framework provides a consistent construction of gravitational vertices for massive fields of arbitrary integer and half-integer spin, incorporating both minimal and non-minimal terms to ensure gauge invariance, with verification through specific spin cases and their partially massless limits.

title: Rephasing invariant structure of CP phase for simplified mixing matrices in Fritzsch--Xing parametrization
summary:
In this paper, we construct an explicit rephasing transformation that converts an arbitrary unitary mixing matrix into the Fritzsch--Xing (FX) parametrization, which is obtained by trivializing arguments of the matrix elements in the third row and third column. We further analyzed the rephasing invariant structure of the FX phase $δ_{\rm FX}$ under the approximation where the 1-3 element of the diagonalization matrix of charged leptons $U^{e}$ is neglected, $U_{13}^{e} = 0$. As a result, in the limit where the 1-3 element of diagonalization of neutrinos $U^ν$ is also neglected,
  we obtained a compact expression for the FX phase $δ_{\rm FX} = \arg [ { U^{e}_{11} U^{e}_{12} U^{e}_{33} } { U^{ν*}_{11} U^{ν*}_{12} U^{ν*}_{33} / \det U^{e} \det U^{ν*} } ] - \arg [ 1 + ({U^{e *}_{23} U^ν_{23} / U^{e *}_{33} U^ν_{33}} ) ] $. In this limit, the FX phase is controlled by two independent relative phases between $U^{ν, e}$, and the FX phase for finite $U_{13}^ν$ is understood as a generalization to the compact expression.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs an explicit rephasing transformation to convert any unitary mixing matrix into the Fritzsch-Xing parametrization, analyzes the rephasing invariant structure of the FX phase δ_FX under approximations, and derives a compact expression for δ_FX in the limit where certain matrix elements are neglected.
AI.motivation: To establish a systematic connection between arbitrary unitary mixing matrices and the Fritzsch-Xing parametrization, which trivializes phases in the third row and third column, and to understand the rephasing invariant structure of the FX phase δ_FX under physically motivated approximations.
AI.method: Construct an explicit rephasing transformation that converts any unitary mixing matrix into the FX parametrization. Analyze the rephasing invariant structure of δ_FX under the approximation U^e_13 = 0, and derive expressions for δ_FX in the limit where U^ν_13 is also neglected, obtaining a compact formula involving elements of charged lepton and neutrino diagonalization matrices.
AI.result: Successfully constructed the rephasing transformation to FX parametrization. Derived a compact expression for δ_FX = arg[U^e_11 U^e_12 U^e_33 U^ν*_11 U^ν*_12 U^ν*_33/(det U^e det U^ν*)] - arg[1 + (U^e*_23 U^ν_23/(U^e*_33 U^ν_33))] in the limit U^e_13 = U^ν_13 = 0. Showed that δ_FX is controlled by two independent relative phases between U^ν and U^e, and that the finite U^ν_13 case is a generalization of this compact expression.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a systematic framework for connecting arbitrary unitary mixing matrices to the FX parametrization and clarifies the rephasing invariant structure of the FX phase. The derived compact expression for δ_FX under reasonable approximations offers insights into how the phase is determined by elements of charged lepton and neutrino diagonalization matrices, with the finite U^ν_13 case representing a natural generalization.

title: Black holes from the gravitational path integral: supersymmetric indices and precision holography
comment: PhD thesis. Based on the author's contributions: 2208.01007, 2304.06101, 2403.02410, 2409.01332, 2507.12650. 280 pages + appendices and references. 8 figures
summary: The counting of microstates of supersymmetric black holes with anti-de Sitter or flat asymptotics is obtained by computing a supersymmetric index in a weakly coupled string theory or a dual superconformal field theory. These indices are protected observables, whose value can be reliably extrapolated from weak to strong coupling, where the gravitational description applies. In this Thesis, after a broad introductory review, we discuss recent progress in formulating such protected observables directly within the gravitational theory, via the Euclidean path integral. In the semiclassical limit the index reduces to a sum over complex Euclidean saddles. These saddles are supersymmetric but ''non-extremal'', and arise in both anti-de Sitter and flat spaces. In the holographic setting, we investigate four-derivative corrections to the thermodynamics of AdS$_5$ black holes. Using off-shell methods, we construct the corrected action of five-dimensional gauged supergravity. We then evaluate the corrected on-shell action of supersymmetric AdS$_5$ black holes and find exact agreement with a Cardy-like limit of the superconformal index of the dual conformal field theory. By a Legendre transform of the action, we obtain the corrected black hole entropy, and we confirm this result by applying Wald's formula to the corrected near-horizon geometry. We then turn to the gravitational index with asymptotically flat boundary conditions. We uncover a broad family of novel saddles and present a general classification based on their rod structure, which characterizes their topology. These solutions may feature multiple horizons or three-dimensional bubbles with lens space topology, and allowing for conical singularities yields further geometries, involving spindles and branched spheres. For the simpler geometries, the on-shell action is computed using an odd-dimensional version of equivariant localization.

AI.tldr: Thesis develops gravitational path integral approach to compute supersymmetric black hole indices directly in gravity theory, covering both AdS and flat asymptotics, with applications to holographic thermodynamics and classification of novel Euclidean saddles.
AI.motivation: To formulate protected observables (supersymmetric indices) directly within gravitational theory via Euclidean path integral, enabling computation of black hole microstate counting without relying on weakly coupled string theory or dual field theory descriptions.
AI.method: Uses Euclidean path integral approach in semiclassical limit, reducing index to sum over complex Euclidean saddles. For AdS: constructs corrected action of 5D gauged supergravity with four-derivative terms, evaluates on-shell action via off-shell methods. For flat space: classifies novel saddles by rod structure, computes on-shell action using odd-dimensional equivariant localization.
AI.result: For AdS: exact agreement found between corrected gravitational on-shell action and Cardy-like limit of dual CFT superconformal index; corrected black hole entropy obtained via Legendre transform and confirmed by Wald's formula. For flat space: broad family of novel saddles discovered with classification by topology (multiple horizons, 3D bubbles with lens space topology, spindles, branched spheres).
AI.conclusion: Thesis demonstrates successful formulation of supersymmetric indices directly in gravitational theory via Euclidean path integral, establishing precise holographic matching including higher-derivative corrections and uncovering rich landscape of Euclidean saddles for flat-space black holes.

title: Dominant One-Loop Seesaw Contribution Induced by Non-Invertible Fusion Algebra
summary: The topological classification of the one-loop Weinberg operator at dimension-5 enables a systematic categorization of radiative neutrino mass models. Among these, the category consisting loop-extended seesaw frameworks is theoretically appealing but conventional discrete or continuous symmetries (\emph{e.g.}, $U(1)$ or $\mathbb{Z}_M$) cannot genuinely forbid the corresponding tree-level contributions, making loop dominance difficult to realize. We show that \textit{non-invertible selection rules} (NISRs) naturally enforce the absence of tree-level terms while ensuring a dominant one-loop contribution. Intriguingly, the same non-invertible structure also stabilizes the dark matter candidate, providing a unified radiative origin of neutrino mass and dark sector stability. In particular, we focus on the T4-2-$i$ topology which embodies a type-II one-loop seesaw and demonstrate its natural realization from $Z_{7}$ Tambara--Yamagami (TY) fusion algebra.

AI.tldr: Non-invertible selection rules from Tambara-Yamagami fusion algebra naturally enforce loop dominance in radiative neutrino mass models while simultaneously stabilizing dark matter candidates.
AI.motivation: Conventional symmetries (discrete or continuous) cannot genuinely forbid tree-level contributions in loop-extended seesaw frameworks, making loop dominance difficult to achieve. There is a need for new symmetry structures that can enforce the absence of tree-level terms while ensuring dominant loop contributions.
AI.method: Utilize non-invertible selection rules (NISRs) from Tambara-Yamagami fusion algebra, specifically focusing on the T4-2-i topology which embodies a type-II one-loop seesaw. Demonstrate natural realization from Z7 Tambara-Yamagami fusion algebra to enforce loop dominance and dark matter stability.
AI.result: Non-invertible selection rules naturally enforce the absence of tree-level contributions while ensuring dominant one-loop neutrino mass generation. The same non-invertible structure simultaneously stabilizes dark matter candidates, providing a unified framework for radiative neutrino mass origin and dark matter stability.
AI.conclusion: Non-invertible symmetries offer a powerful alternative to conventional symmetries for enforcing loop dominance in radiative neutrino mass models, with the added benefit of naturally stabilizing dark matter, creating a unified framework for neutrino mass generation and dark matter stability.

title: Defect relative entropy in symmetric orbifold CFTs
summary:
In this work, we compute the defect relative entropy between topological defects in the symmetric product orbifold CFT $\mathrm{Sym}^N(M) = M^{\otimes N}/S_N$. Our analysis covers two distinct classes of defects: universal defects, which realize the $\mathrm{Rep}(S_N)$ non-invertible symmetry, and non-universal defects.
  We show that the defect relative entropy reduces to a Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence. The resulting expression decomposes naturally into two contributions: one governed by characters of the symmetric group $S_N$, and the other controlled by modular $S$-matrix elements of the seed RCFT. Remarkably, both sets of data appear as probability distributions, yielding an information-theoretic interpretation of permutation group data and modular data within the symmetric orbifold.
  The structure of the divergence depends sensitively on the defect class. For universal defects, only the permutation group data contributes; for maximally fractional defects, both permutation and modular data enter and together define the relevant probability distributions. This feature suggests that the maximally fractional defect can be understood as a kind of product of the RCFT defect and the symmetric orbifold defect.

AI.tldr: Defect relative entropy in symmetric product orbifold CFT reduces to KL divergence with contributions from symmetric group characters and modular S-matrix elements, interpreted as probability distributions.
AI.motivation: To compute and understand defect relative entropy between topological defects in symmetric product orbifold CFTs, particularly distinguishing between universal defects (realizing Rep(S_N) non-invertible symmetry) and non-universal defects, and to provide information-theoretic interpretation of permutation group and modular data.
AI.method: Compute defect relative entropy in symmetric product orbifold CFT Sym^N(M) = M^⊗N/S_N, analyzing two defect classes: universal defects and non-universal defects. Show reduction to Kullback-Leibler divergence with decomposition into contributions from symmetric group S_N characters and modular S-matrix elements of seed RCFT.
AI.result: Defect relative entropy reduces to KL divergence with two contributions: one from S_N characters and one from modular S-matrix elements, both appearing as probability distributions. For universal defects, only permutation group data contributes; for maximally fractional defects, both permutation and modular data enter, suggesting these defects can be understood as products of RCFT and symmetric orbifold defects.
AI.conclusion: The defect relative entropy provides an information-theoretic framework that interprets symmetric group characters and modular S-matrix elements as probability distributions, revealing structural differences between defect classes and suggesting product structure for maximally fractional defects.

title: Revisiting charmonium hybrid spectroscopy
summary: Hadrons with explicit gluonic degrees of freedom, such as charmonium hybrids, are key to understanding nonperturbative behavior of strong interaction, yet they remain experimentally elusive. Within a constituent gluon model treating the hybrid as a $c\bar{c}g$ three-body system with a transverse electric gluon, we predict the masses of the lightest hybrid multiplet ($J^{PC}=1^{--}, 0^{-+}, 1^{-+}, 2^{-+}$) to lie in the range $4.19$--$4.32$ GeV. By analyzing their decay patterns, we provide specific, experimentally testable signatures to guide the search for these exotic states at current and future facilities.

AI.tldr: The paper predicts masses and decay patterns of charmonium hybrids (c\bar{c}g) to guide experimental searches for these exotic hadrons with explicit gluonic degrees of freedom.
AI.motivation: Hadrons with explicit gluonic degrees of freedom, particularly charmonium hybrids, are crucial for understanding nonperturbative QCD behavior but remain experimentally elusive. There is a need to provide specific, testable signatures to guide experimental searches at current and future facilities.
AI.method: The authors use a constituent gluon model treating the hybrid as a three-body c\bar{c}g system with a transverse electric gluon. They predict masses of the lightest hybrid multiplet and analyze their decay patterns.
AI.result: The predicted masses for the lightest hybrid multiplet (J^{PC}=1^{--}, 0^{-+}, 1^{-+}, 2^{-+}) lie in the range 4.19-4.32 GeV. The analysis provides specific, experimentally testable decay signatures to guide searches.
AI.conclusion: The study offers concrete predictions for charmonium hybrid masses and decay patterns, providing valuable guidance for experimental searches that could finally reveal these elusive exotic hadrons with explicit gluonic degrees of freedom.

title: Jackiw-Teitelboim Gravity from Holonomies: Discrete BF Formulation and Boundary Symmetries
summary: We develop a fully discrete and non-perturbative formulation of two-dimensional Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity within the BF framework. Using group-valued holonomies and Lie-algebra--valued dilatons, the bulk theory is shown to be purely topological, with all physical information encoded at the boundary. We analyze admissible discrete boundary conditions and derive the corresponding asymptotic symmetry algebras directly at the lattice level, including an affine Kac-Moody symmetry and its Brown-Henneaux reduction to a Virasoro algebra, together with the associated Virasoro-dilaton structure. A precise operator product expansion (OPE) dictionary is established by taking the controlled continuum limit of the discrete Poisson brackets. Beyond asymptotic symmetries, we provide an effective boundary description and a representation-theoretic quantization organized by monodromy sectors. Within this discrete framework, black hole entropy follows from gauge-invariant holonomy data and is expressed in terms of the dilaton Casimir, reproducing the Bekenstein--Hawking result without invoking a fundamental Schwarzian action.

AI.tldr: Non-perturbative discrete formulation of 2D JT gravity in BF framework with group-valued holonomies and Lie-algebra-valued dilatons, deriving asymptotic symmetries, establishing OPE dictionary, and obtaining black hole entropy from gauge-invariant holonomy data.
AI.motivation: Develop a fully discrete, non-perturbative formulation of 2D Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity to understand its fundamental structure beyond continuum approximations, particularly focusing on boundary physics and black hole entropy derivation without relying on Schwarzian actions.
AI.method: Use BF framework with group-valued holonomies and Lie-algebra-valued dilatons; analyze discrete boundary conditions; derive asymptotic symmetry algebras at lattice level; establish OPE dictionary via continuum limit of discrete Poisson brackets; employ representation-theoretic quantization organized by monodromy sectors.
AI.result: Derived affine Kac-Moody symmetry and its Brown-Henneaux reduction to Virasoro algebra with Virasoro-dilaton structure; established precise OPE dictionary; obtained black hole entropy from gauge-invariant holonomy data expressed in terms of dilaton Casimir, reproducing Bekenstein-Hawking result without fundamental Schwarzian action.
AI.conclusion: The discrete BF formulation provides a complete non-perturbative framework for 2D JT gravity where bulk is purely topological, all physics resides at boundary, and black hole entropy emerges naturally from gauge-invariant holonomy data, offering insights beyond continuum approximations.

title: Dark higher-form fields and triangle anomalies
summary: Light scalar and vector particles admit non-trivial descriptions in terms of anti-symmetric higher-rank tensor fields. Far from mere rewritings, these provide compelling alternative frameworks, leading to immediate phenomenological applications. In this paper, we extend the playground to include the contributions of fermionic triangle loops, and use these results to compare the standard and higher-form realizations for two phenomenological processes: the pair production of two dark particles and the decay of a dark particle in two photons. Though they all do show some dependencies on the chosen realizations for the spin-zero or the spin-one dark states, we find that the two-photon mode is particularly sensitive and could actually be our prime window into the true nature of the dark field.

AI.tldr: Higher-rank tensor field descriptions of scalar/vector particles enable alternative frameworks with distinct phenomenology, particularly in fermionic triangle loop contributions to dark particle production and decay processes.
AI.motivation: To explore how alternative higher-form realizations of scalar and vector particles (as anti-symmetric higher-rank tensor fields) affect phenomenological predictions, particularly when including fermionic triangle loop contributions, and to identify which processes are most sensitive to these different theoretical descriptions.
AI.method: Extends the analysis of higher-form realizations to include fermionic triangle loop contributions, then compares standard and higher-form descriptions for two key phenomenological processes: dark particle pair production and dark particle decay into two photons.
AI.result: All processes show dependencies on the chosen realization (standard vs. higher-form) for spin-zero and spin-one dark states, but the two-photon decay mode is particularly sensitive and could serve as the primary probe into the true nature of the dark field.
AI.conclusion: The two-photon decay channel offers enhanced sensitivity to distinguish between standard and higher-form descriptions of dark particles, potentially revealing the fundamental nature of dark fields through their coupling to photons via fermionic loops.

title: Resummation of small-spin singularities in anomalous dimensions of twist-two operators
summary: Anomalous dimensions of leading-twist operators in QCD play an important role in precision predictions for high-energy processes, since they govern the scale evolution of parton distributions. Their analytic structure as a function of spin is particularly important due to the complexity of higher-loop computations. In these proceedings, we discuss the resummation of the certain type of such singularities that share common features with those appearing in the quark flavor-nonsinglet sector of QCD. Our main focus is on the interplay between Gross-Neveu-Yukawa model in $ε$ expansion and Gross-Neveu in $1/N$ expansion. Such resummation allows one to predict the higher-loop singular behavior and reveals connections with the conformal Regge theory and recent studies of detector operators in QCD and various conformal field theories.

AI.tldr: Resummation of singularities in anomalous dimensions of leading-twist QCD operators using Gross-Neveu model expansions to predict higher-loop behavior and reveal connections with conformal Regge theory.
AI.motivation: Anomalous dimensions of leading-twist operators in QCD are crucial for precision predictions in high-energy processes as they govern scale evolution of parton distributions. Their analytic structure as a function of spin is important due to the complexity of higher-loop computations.
AI.method: Resummation of certain singularities in anomalous dimensions using interplay between Gross-Neveu-Yukawa model in ε expansion and Gross-Neveu model in 1/N expansion. This approach allows prediction of higher-loop singular behavior.
AI.result: The resummation technique enables prediction of higher-loop singular behavior and reveals connections with conformal Regge theory and recent studies of detector operators in QCD and various conformal field theories.
AI.conclusion: The interplay between different expansions of Gross-Neveu models provides a powerful approach for resumming singularities in anomalous dimensions, connecting QCD calculations with broader conformal field theory frameworks and Regge theory.

title: Gauge-independent gravitational waves from a minimal dark $U(1)$ sector with viable dark matter candidates
summary: Searches for stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds from first-order phase transitions offer a powerful probe of hidden sectors, but quantitative predictions in gauge theories are obstructed by the gauge dependence of the finite-temperature effective potential and the associated tunneling action. We study a minimal gauged $U(1)$ dark sector containing a dark Higgs and a dark photon, optionally supplemented by a vectorlike dark fermion, coupled to the Standard Model through Higgs portal or kinetic mixing. Using the Nielsen identity together with a controlled derivative expansion and power counting, we construct a gauge-independent effective action in the high- and low-temperature limits, enabling model-intrinsic nucleation dynamics and robust gravitational wave predictions. We perform dedicated Monte Carlo scans in both limits and map viable microscopic parameters to detector-facing peak frequencies and amplitudes, spanning bands relevant to pulsar timing arrays and planned space-based interferometers. In our scans, supercooled transitions typically produce the strongest signals, whereas parametrically high-temperature transitions are comparatively rare and tend to be weak. We further connect the phase transition phenomenology to viable dark matter candidates within the same minimal field content, providing benchmark targets for dark photon dark matter and dark fermion dark matter, and highlighting their complementarity with gravitational wave observables. Overall, our results provide an end-to-end, gauge-independent pipeline from a minimal hidden sector Lagrangian to gravitational wave spectra and cosmologically viable dark matter benchmarks, yielding the most reliable and concrete predictions to date for a minimal gauged $U(1)$ dark sector.

AI.tldr: Gauge-independent analysis of gravitational wave signals from first-order phase transitions in minimal U(1) dark sectors, connecting to dark matter candidates and experimental observables.
AI.motivation: Gauge dependence obstructs quantitative predictions of gravitational wave backgrounds from first-order phase transitions in gauge theories, necessitating a gauge-independent framework for reliable predictions in minimal dark sectors.
AI.method: Use Nielsen identity with controlled derivative expansion and power counting to construct gauge-independent effective action in high- and low-temperature limits; perform Monte Carlo scans to map microscopic parameters to gravitational wave observables.
AI.result: Supercooled transitions produce strongest gravitational wave signals, while high-temperature transitions are rare and weak; viable dark matter benchmarks identified for dark photon and dark fermion candidates, with complementarity to gravitational wave observables.
AI.conclusion: Provides first end-to-end, gauge-independent pipeline from minimal hidden sector Lagrangian to gravitational wave spectra and cosmologically viable dark matter benchmarks, offering most reliable predictions for minimal gauged U(1) dark sectors.

title: Integral Transformations for Conformally Invariant Celestial Gluon Amplitudes
summary: We propose an integral transformation for celestial gluon amplitudes that maps the celestial coordinates \((z_i,\bar z_i)\) to a new set of complex variables \((s_i,\bar s_i)\), inspired by the structure of closed string scattering amplitudes. A consistent inverse transformation is constructed by regulating a divergence associated with translational redundancy and absorbing it into an overall normalization. Applying this transformation to celestial MHV amplitudes, we derive constraints on \((s_i,\bar s_i)\) for three-, four-, and general \(n\)-point amplitudes, and show that these conditions are necessary for invariance under global conformal transformations.

AI.tldr: Proposes an integral transformation for celestial gluon amplitudes mapping celestial coordinates to new complex variables inspired by closed string amplitudes, with consistent inverse via regularization, and derives constraints ensuring global conformal invariance.
AI.motivation: To develop a transformation for celestial amplitudes that connects celestial coordinates to new variables inspired by string theory, enabling analysis of global conformal invariance properties.
AI.method: Proposes an integral transformation mapping celestial coordinates (z_i, \bar z_i) to new complex variables (s_i, \bar s_i) inspired by closed string scattering amplitudes. Constructs consistent inverse transformation by regularizing a divergence from translational redundancy and absorbing it into overall normalization.
AI.result: Derives constraints on (s_i, \bar s_i) for three-, four-, and general n-point MHV amplitudes. Shows these conditions are necessary for invariance under global conformal transformations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed transformation successfully maps celestial amplitudes to new variables with constraints ensuring global conformal invariance, establishing a connection between celestial amplitudes and string-inspired mathematical structures.

title: Parapositronium decay into three photons and implications for the neutral pion
summary: We complete the determination of the parapositronium decay into three photons by evaluating amplitudes mediated by the $Z$ boson. We show that, contrary to the expectation that the extra mass scale $m_e$ may bring an enhancement to the overall scaling, the amplitude turns out to start at $1/m_Z^6$ order, similarly to the $W$ boson mediated amplitude. The decay rate with both $W$ and $Z$ boson contributions is found to be $1.1\cdot 10^{-80}$ eV, about 47 orders of magnitude smaller than previously estimated. We also discuss its implication for the $π^0\to3γ$ amplitude.

AI.tldr: The paper completes parapositronium decay into three photons calculation including Z boson contributions, finding unexpectedly small amplitude scaling and dramatically reduced decay rate compared to previous estimates.
AI.motivation: To complete the theoretical determination of parapositronium decay into three photons by evaluating amplitudes mediated by the Z boson, addressing previous incomplete calculations and testing expectations about mass scale enhancements.
AI.method: Evaluation of quantum field theory amplitudes for parapositronium decay into three photons mediated by Z boson exchange, comparing scaling behavior with W boson mediated amplitudes, and calculating the total decay rate including both contributions.
AI.result: Z boson mediated amplitude starts at 1/m_Z^6 order (same as W boson), contrary to expectations of enhancement from extra mass scale m_e. Total decay rate with both W and Z contributions is 1.1×10^{-80} eV, about 47 orders of magnitude smaller than previous estimates.
AI.conclusion: The completed calculation reveals parapositronium decay into three photons is extremely suppressed, with Z boson contributions following similar scaling as W boson. The dramatic reduction compared to previous estimates has implications for understanding similar processes like π^0→3γ.

title: Quantum criticality and mixed-state entanglement in holographic superconductor--insulator transitions
summary: We study quantum criticality in a holographic Einstein--Maxwell--Dilaton--Axion (EMDA) p-wave superconductor exhibiting a superconductor--insulator transition (SIT). By tracking the superconducting energy gap, we show that approaching the quantum critical point (QCP) closes the gap and induces incipient insulating features, indicating that enhanced quantum fluctuations suppress superconducting order and trigger the SIT. To probe the transition, we employ two holographic indicators: holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and the entanglement wedge cross-section (EWCS), the latter being a mixed-state entanglement measure. In contrast to HEE, which for sufficiently large configuration is dominated by the thermal entropy and is therefore largely insensitive to entanglement along the temperature direction, EWCS displays pronounced critical scaling and provides a robust diagnostic of the quantum phase transition (QPT). We attribute this contrast to the fact that HEE at large scales is controlled by the infrared (IR) geometry, whereas EWCS is governed by deformations of the entire bulk. Our results establish EWCS as a robust probe of holographic quantum criticality in mixed states.

AI.tldr: Holographic study of p-wave superconductor-insulator transition using entanglement measures shows EWCS is superior to HEE for detecting quantum criticality in mixed states.
AI.motivation: To understand quantum criticality in holographic p-wave superconductors undergoing superconductor-insulator transitions and identify robust entanglement measures for detecting quantum phase transitions in mixed states.
AI.method: Employ holographic Einstein-Maxwell-Dilaton-Axion model to study p-wave superconductor, track superconducting energy gap, and use two holographic entanglement measures: holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and entanglement wedge cross-section (EWCS).
AI.result: Approaching quantum critical point closes superconducting gap and induces insulating features; EWCS shows pronounced critical scaling and robustly detects quantum phase transition, while HEE is dominated by thermal entropy and insensitive to entanglement along temperature direction.
AI.conclusion: EWCS is established as a robust probe of holographic quantum criticality in mixed states, superior to HEE for detecting quantum phase transitions due to its sensitivity to bulk deformations rather than just IR geometry.

title: Probing Quark Electric Dipole Moment with Topological Anomalies
summary: CP-odd observables are identified in $γ^*\to K^+K^-π^0$ and evaluated in the chiral limit. A nonzero T-odd asymmetry $A_T$ requires anomalous couplings descending from a five-dimensional Chern-Simons construction. Modeling the running of $F_A$ and $F_V$ with the vector meson dominance, we estimate sensitivities to the strange-quark EDM: $\mathcal{O}(10^{-16}),e\cdot\mathrm{cm}$ in $e^+e^-$ data at VEPP-2000 (CMD-3) and $\mathcal{O}(10^{-18}),e\cdot\mathrm{cm}$ using existing $J/ψ$ samples at BESIII. Future experiments in the Super Tau-Charm Facility and Belle II can further improve the reach by an order of magnitude.
