AI.tldr: The paper identifies CP-odd observables in γ*→K⁺K⁻π⁰ decays and evaluates them in the chiral limit, estimating sensitivities to strange-quark electric dipole moments using various experimental facilities.
AI.motivation: To probe CP violation beyond the Standard Model by measuring strange-quark electric dipole moments (EDMs) through CP-odd observables in radiative decays, which require anomalous couplings from higher-dimensional operators.
AI.method: Identification of CP-odd observables in γ*→K⁺K⁻π⁰ decays, evaluation in the chiral limit, modeling of form factor running using vector meson dominance, and estimation of experimental sensitivities using various collider data.
AI.result: A nonzero T-odd asymmetry A_T requires anomalous couplings from five-dimensional Chern-Simons construction. Estimated sensitivities: O(10⁻¹⁶) e·cm using e⁺e⁻ data at VEPP-2000/CMD-3, O(10⁻¹⁸) e·cm using existing J/ψ samples at BESIII, with potential order-of-magnitude improvements from future experiments.
AI.conclusion: CP-odd observables in γ*→K⁺K⁻π⁰ decays provide a promising avenue to probe strange-quark EDMs, with current and future experimental facilities offering competitive sensitivity to new physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Holographic Subregion Complexity and Fidelity Susceptibility in Noncommutative Yang--Mills Theory
summary: We analyze the behavior of holographic subregion complexity (HSC) and holographic fidelity susceptibility (HFS) in noncommutative Yang--Mills theory. The emergence of a minimum length scale, dictated by the degree of noncommutativity, induces a behavioral transition in the HSC and establishes a lower bound. In the large noncommutativity regime, the qualitative features of the complexity deviate significantly from the commutative case. The HFS is shown to provide an effective measure of the degree of noncommutativity. Although the HSC generally satisfies strong subadditivity, this property fails abruptly when the subregion size approaches the minimum length scale. At finite temperature, the long-range behavior of the HSC is modified, and its lower bound scales positively with temperature. Furthermore, temperature enhances the sensitivity of the fidelity susceptibility to the degree of noncommutativity. Within the AdS soliton background, a competition between connected and disconnected configurations arises in the HSC, signaling a phase-transition-like behavior. Finally, the compactification scale is found to diminish the sensitivity of the HFS to the degree of noncommutativity.

AI.tldr: Holographic subregion complexity and fidelity susceptibility in noncommutative Yang-Mills theory show modified behavior due to minimum length scale, with complexity exhibiting lower bounds, strong subadditivity violation near minimum scale, and temperature-dependent properties.
AI.motivation: To understand how noncommutative geometry affects holographic complexity measures, particularly how the minimum length scale induced by noncommutativity modifies the behavior of holographic subregion complexity and fidelity susceptibility in Yang-Mills theory.
AI.method: Analysis of holographic subregion complexity (HSC) and holographic fidelity susceptibility (HFS) in noncommutative Yang-Mills theory using gauge/gravity duality, examining effects of noncommutativity parameter, temperature, and compactification in various backgrounds including AdS soliton.
AI.result: Noncommutativity introduces minimum length scale causing behavioral transition in HSC with lower bound; HFS effectively measures noncommutativity degree; HSC violates strong subadditivity near minimum scale; temperature modifies HSC long-range behavior and enhances HFS sensitivity; AdS soliton shows phase-transition-like behavior; compactification reduces HFS sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: Noncommutative geometry fundamentally alters holographic complexity measures, with minimum length scale inducing novel features including lower bounds, subadditivity violations, and temperature-dependent scaling, while fidelity susceptibility serves as effective probe of noncommutativity degree.

title: Inclusive hadroproduction of $χ_{c1}(3872)$, $X_b$ and pentaquarks
summary: We use the Born--Oppenheimer effective field theory factorization to compute the inclusive production cross sections of the $χ_{c1}(3872)$ and its partner in the bottomonium sector. In the same framework, we compute the production cross sections of the pentaquark states $P_{c\bar{c}}(4312)^+$, $P_{c\bar{c}}(4457)^+$, $P_{c\bar{c}}(4380)^+$ and $P_{c\bar{c}}(4440)^+$ within two possible scenarios for the Born--Oppenheimer potentials. Also for pentaquarks, we extend the results to the bottomonium sector. All our results are genuine predictions that do not involve fits to prompt hadroproduction data.

AI.tldr: Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory used to compute inclusive production cross sections for χc1(3872), its bottomonium partner, and four pentaquark states in both charm and bottom sectors without fitting to hadroproduction data.
AI.motivation: To provide first-principles predictions for production cross sections of exotic hadrons (χc1(3872) and pentaquark states) using a consistent theoretical framework without relying on experimental data fits.
AI.method: Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory factorization approach applied to compute inclusive production cross sections. Two possible scenarios for Born-Oppenheimer potentials considered for pentaquark calculations.
AI.result: Computed production cross sections for χc1(3872), its bottomonium partner, and four pentaquark states (Pc̅c(4312)+, Pc̅c(4457)+, Pc̅c(4380)+, Pc̅c(4440)+) in both charm and bottom sectors.
AI.conclusion: The study provides genuine theoretical predictions for exotic hadron production cross sections using Born-Oppenheimer EFT, offering testable results for experimental verification without data fitting.

title: Flavor dependence of chiral symmetry breaking and the conformal window
summary: We investigate the phase structure of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) in the vacuum as a function of quark flavor number $N_f$ within the chiral limit. By self-consistently solving the coupled DSEs for the quark and gluon propagators in a minimal QCD scheme, we elucidate the nonperturbative dynamics governing dynamical chiral symmetry breaking. Our calculations determine a critical flavor number of $N_f^c=6.81$ which marks the chiral symmetry restoration of quarks. Further analysis reveals the critical exponents of the chiral condensate as $ -\langle\barψ ψ\rangle\sim |N_f-N_f^c|^{0.53(9)}$, characterized the second order feature of this phase transition of chiral symmetry. Additionally, we discuss the implications for the walking regime towards the conformal window at larger flavor.

AI.tldr: The paper determines the critical flavor number N_f^c=6.81 for chiral symmetry restoration in QCD using Dyson-Schwinger equations, revealing a second-order phase transition with critical exponent 0.53(9).
AI.motivation: To investigate the phase structure of QCD in the vacuum as a function of quark flavor number N_f within the chiral limit, and to understand the nonperturbative dynamics governing dynamical chiral symmetry breaking.
AI.method: Self-consistently solving the coupled Dyson-Schwinger equations (DSEs) for the quark and gluon propagators in a minimal QCD scheme.
AI.result: Critical flavor number N_f^c=6.81 marks chiral symmetry restoration; critical exponent of chiral condensate is 0.53(9), characterizing a second-order phase transition; implications for walking regime toward conformal window at larger flavor.
AI.conclusion: The study provides quantitative determination of the critical flavor number for chiral symmetry restoration in QCD, revealing the second-order nature of the phase transition and offering insights into the transition to conformal behavior at larger flavor numbers.

title: Resurgent structure of the 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole
summary: In this letter we present a comprehensive analysis of the differential equations governing the spatial profile of the 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole from the viewpoint of resurgence theory. We note that the special shape of the gauge-component asymptotics, together with the simplicity of its Borel transform and the Green's kernels in the Volterra equations, provides a complete control over the proliferation of the Borel-plane singularities to all orders and for any $λ/e^2>0$, along with full information about the relevant logarithmic discontinuities. Hence, the resurgent structure of the non-BPS solutions turns out to be unexpectedly simple, and its resonance at the origin of the Borel plane even admits an analytic calculation of the normalization coefficients of their asymptotic forms to an arbitrary level of precision.

AI.tldr: Resurgence theory analysis reveals unexpectedly simple structure of 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole differential equations with complete control over Borel-plane singularities and analytic calculation of asymptotic normalization coefficients.
AI.motivation: To analyze the differential equations governing the spatial profile of the 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole from the perspective of resurgence theory, understanding the resurgent structure of non-BPS solutions.
AI.method: Comprehensive resurgence theory analysis leveraging the special shape of gauge-component asymptotics, simplicity of Borel transforms, and Green's kernels in Volterra equations to control Borel-plane singularities and logarithmic discontinuities.
AI.result: Complete control over proliferation of Borel-plane singularities to all orders for any λ/e²>0, with full information about relevant logarithmic discontinuities. The resurgent structure is unexpectedly simple, and resonance at Borel plane origin allows analytic calculation of asymptotic normalization coefficients to arbitrary precision.
AI.conclusion: The 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole exhibits a remarkably simple resurgent structure despite being non-BPS, enabling unprecedented analytic control over asymptotic behavior and normalization coefficients through resurgence theory techniques.

title: S-matrices in the holomorphic modular bootstrap approach
comment: 18 pages, 1 figure, Appendix by Abhiram Kidambi; A Mathematica notebook with many more examples is provided as an ancillary file
summary: We numerically determine the S-matrix by using connection formulae in the modular linear differential equation (MLDE) approach to the holomorphic modular bootstrap. We then determine exact formulae using the fact that entries in the $S$-matrix are integer entries in a cyclotomic extension of the field of rational numbers. This provides a method that is intrinsic to the MLDE setup and does not require inputs outside this framework. The method is illustrated with a selection of examples.

AI.tldr: Numerical determination of S-matrix via MLDE connection formulae, followed by exact formula derivation using integer entries in cyclotomic extensions, providing an intrinsic MLDE method without external inputs.
AI.motivation: To develop an intrinsic method within the modular linear differential equation (MLDE) framework for determining exact S-matrices in holomorphic modular bootstrap, avoiding reliance on external inputs.
AI.method: Use connection formulae in MLDE approach to numerically determine S-matrix, then derive exact formulae by exploiting that S-matrix entries are integers in cyclotomic extensions of rational numbers.
AI.result: Successfully determined exact S-matrices using purely MLDE-based approach, demonstrated through selection of examples showing the method's effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: Developed an intrinsic MLDE method for exact S-matrix determination that operates entirely within the MLDE framework without requiring external inputs, validated through example applications.

title: Light dilaton from top-down holographic confinement with magnetic fluxes
summary: A two-parameter class of higher-dimensional, strongly coupled, confining field theories in the presence of magnetic fluxes for two Abelian gauge groups admits a top-down, holographic dual description. The corresponding two-parameter family of regular background solutions of the classical equations of maximal supergravity in seven dimensions descends from maximal supergravity in eleven dimensions. We study the global and local stability properties of these solutions. We identify lines of zero-temperature first-order phase transitions, describing a polygon (a square) in the space of parameters, identified with the two fluxes. In the spectrum of fluctuations of the supergravity equations, interpreted as bound states of the dual, confining field theories, we find no evidence of local instabilities (tachyons). Over a significant portion of parameter space, that extends far away from the proximity to the transition, we identify an approximate dilaton, the mass of which is one order of magnitude smaller than the scale set by confinement. Our findings complement those emerging in other holographic models discussed in the literature, in which either the dilaton mass is only mildly lower than the confinement scale (when approaching a first-order transitions), or parametrically suppressed (when reaching the proximity to a second-order one).

AI.tldr: Holographic study of 2-parameter confining field theories with magnetic fluxes reveals first-order phase transitions forming a square in flux space, with no tachyonic instabilities and an approximate dilaton with mass significantly below confinement scale.
AI.motivation: To investigate stability properties of higher-dimensional, strongly coupled confining field theories with magnetic fluxes using their top-down holographic dual description derived from maximal supergravity.
AI.method: Study a two-parameter family of regular background solutions in seven-dimensional maximal supergravity (descending from 11D supergravity) using holographic duality; analyze global and local stability by examining fluctuation spectra and phase transitions.
AI.result: Identified lines of zero-temperature first-order phase transitions forming a square in the two-flux parameter space; found no evidence of local instabilities (tachyons) in fluctuation spectra; discovered an approximate dilaton with mass one order of magnitude smaller than confinement scale over significant parameter space.
AI.conclusion: The findings complement other holographic models: while some show mildly suppressed dilaton mass near first-order transitions or parametrically suppressed mass near second-order transitions, this model exhibits significantly suppressed dilaton mass far from transitions, providing new insights into confining gauge theories.

title: On the Unitarity of the Gravitational S-Matrix in High Dimension
summary: We argue that for finite energy windows, the final states in gravitational scattering in dimension $d > 4$ are normalizable coherent states in Fock space. However, as the center of the energy window goes to infinity, black hole physics predicts that these states become orthogonal to every state with a finite number of particles. Given that the spectral measure in energy is determined by Poincare invariance, the S-matrix cannot be a unitary operator in Fock space, despite having finite matrix elements in Fock space, and satisfying perturbative unitarity, to all orders in string perturbation theory. We identify regimes in the BFSS matrix model\cite{bfss} and the definition of the S-matrix as the limit of CFT correlators\cite{polchsuss}, which point to the same conclusion. We review a scattering theory based on the quantum mechanics of a finite number of fermionic oscillators, whose algebra formally converges to the Super-Poincare covariant Awada-Gibbons-Shaw\cite{ags} algebra, and argue that a certain class of limiting states on that algebra satisfy all the properties required by physical unitarity in the algebraic formulation of quantum mechanics. The only missing ingredient for a consistent theory is a proof that the S matrix amplitudes themselves are Poincare invariant. We provide suggestive arguments, but no real proof, that this is so.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that in higher-dimensional gravitational scattering, S-matrix unitarity in Fock space fails due to black hole physics, despite perturbative unitarity in string theory, and proposes an algebraic quantum mechanics framework as a potential resolution.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to resolve the tension between perturbative unitarity in string theory and the non-unitarity of the S-matrix in Fock space predicted by black hole physics in higher-dimensional gravitational scattering, particularly as energy scales approach infinity.
AI.method: The authors analyze gravitational scattering in d>4 dimensions, examine the behavior of coherent states in finite energy windows versus infinite energy limits, study the BFSS matrix model and CFT correlator limits, and review a scattering theory based on fermionic oscillator algebras that converges to the Super-Poincare covariant Awada-Gibbons-Shaw algebra.
AI.result: The paper shows that for finite energy windows, final states are normalizable coherent states in Fock space, but as energy goes to infinity, these states become orthogonal to all finite-particle states, making the S-matrix non-unitary in Fock space despite satisfying perturbative unitarity in string theory. The algebraic quantum mechanics framework provides states satisfying physical unitarity requirements.
AI.conclusion: The S-matrix cannot be unitary in Fock space for gravitational scattering in d>4 due to black hole physics, but an algebraic quantum mechanics approach using fermionic oscillators and the Awada-Gibbons-Shaw algebra offers a potential consistent framework, though Poincare invariance of S-matrix amplitudes remains unproven.
